overview.description: Towie is a three-hand adaptation of bridge invented in Paris in 1931, with only three active players at a time.

history.origins: Towie is documented as a distinct traditional card game with its own player count, equipment, and objective.

rules.objective: Play a bridge-derived trick-taking hand adapted for three active players.
rules.gameplay: Three players are active in each hand, while larger tables rotate participation. Bidding and trick play adapt bridge ideas to the three-hand structure.
keyRules: Invented as a bridge adaptation for three-hand card play.
May be played by more than three players with only three active at one time.

synthesis.shortDescription: Whist is the classic English partnership trick-taking game and ancestor of Bridge. 4 players, 2 teams. 52 cards, 13 each. Last card dealt (to dealer)

prompts.human: Whist is the classic English partnership trick-taking game and ancestor of Bridge. 4 players, 2 teams. 52 cards, 13 each. Last card dealt (to dealer) turned face-up = trump. Eldest hand leads. Follow suit. Each trick over 6 = 1 point. Honours (A-K-Q-J of trump): 3 held = 2pts, 4 held = 4pts. Game to 5 (British) or 7 (American). Rubber = best of 3.
prompts.ai: Game: Whist. Logic: See rules.objective and rules.gameplay.

scoring.description: Odd tricks (over 6) = 1pt each. Honours bonus. Game: 5pts (British) or 7pts (American). Rubber: best of 3 games.
scoring.winCondition: Win majority of tricks. First to 5/7 points.
